entities.name: Quintus Tineius Sacerdos
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Quintus Tineius Sacerdos, a distinguished Roman senator from a prominent Italian senatorial family, achieved two consulships during one of the most tumultuous periods of the Roman Empire, serving as Consul Suffectus in 193 CE and later as Consul Ordinarius in 217 CE. His career provides a vital lens into the resilience and adaptability of the Roman elite amidst the chaotic Year of the Five Emperors and the subsequent establishment of the Severan dynasty. Born into a family already holding consular rank—his father, also Quintus Tineius Sacerdos, was Consul Suffectus in 158 CE—he represented the enduring power of aristocratic lineage in Roman governance, even as the imperial system underwent significant structural changes.

Sacerdos's political trajectory saw him hold several key administrative and military posts, characteristic of a senatorial cursus honorum. Beyond his initial suffect consulship in 193 CE, which occurred during the immediate aftermath of Emperor Commodus's assassination and the subsequent power struggles, he was appointed governor of the senatorial province of Bithynia et Pontus. Later, he achieved the highly prestigious and lucrative governorship of Asia, one of the wealthiest provinces of the empire, before ascending to the ordinary consulship in 217 CE alongside his relative, Publius Maevius Surus. This second consulship, under the reign of Emperor Caracalla, cemented his standing as a leading figure in Roman political life and demonstrated his capacity to maintain influence across successive imperial regimes.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Quintus Tineius Sacerdos's career provides a valuable case study of senatorial resilience and continuity through the turbulent late 2nd and early 3rd centuries CE, including two consulships and major provincial governorships. His family's multi-generational presence in the Roman elite highlights the enduring power of aristocratic networks amidst imperial shifts.
